title: The Five Physical Budgets
summary: Work through The Five Physical Budgets.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Five Physical Budgets** in *The Physical Body* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Physical Body, § The Five Physical Budgets
blocks.md: Every action a learned model proposes ultimately manifests as electrical current flowing through a motor winding, and from that instant physics governs execution. Machine learning practice rarely contends with this transition. Policies trained in simulation typically interact with idealized plants where commanded torque appears instantaneously, heat never accumulates in windings, and direct current (DC) bus voltages never sag under load. A physical machine honors none of these simplifications.

questions.q: The section **The Five Physical Budgets** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Copper loss grows with torque squared, so continuous torque is set by installed heat rejection rather than catalog peak, and a burst spends a stock of heat margin that thermal history has already drawn down.

A torque command is a current that winding inductance and voltage headroom pace and the inverter current limit caps, and a drive can clamp current silently while acknowledging packets, so the safety path must read measured current.

Compute and drives share one DC bus whose impedance turns a coincident current step into droop toward converter lockout while a regenerative stop pumps energy back, so the permission rail is isolated and held up and every unpowered state is specified.
Every physical value carries one of five evidence categories (measured, derived, datasheet, illustrative, chosen), which decides how far an admission decision may rely on it.
